questions.q: Leela in Ahmedabad has a kite string 12 3/10 m long. She cuts two pieces from it, of 3 8/10 m and 5 6/10 m. (a) Find the total length she cut, regrouping tenths into units where needed. (b) Find the length of string left, as a mixed number of units and tenths, borrowing where needed. (c) Check your answer to (b) by writing all the lengths in tenths only. (d) Her brother wants a 3 m piece from what is left. Can she give it? Justify.
questions.a: (a) 3 8/10 + 5 6/10 = 8 + 14/10 = 9 4/10 m. (b) 12 3/10 - 9 4/10: 3 tenths is less than 4 tenths, so split one unit: 11 13/10 - 9 4/10 = 2 9/10 m. (c) 123 tenths - 38 tenths - 56 tenths = 123 - 94 = 29 tenths = 2 9/10 m, the same. (d) No: 2 9/10 m is 29 tenths and 3 m is 30 tenths, so the string left is 1/10 m short.
s: (a) total cut 9 4/10 m, with 14 tenths regrouped as 1 unit and 4 tenths
(b) borrows one unit as 10 tenths (11 13/10) and gets 2 9/10 m left
(c) converts to tenths: 123 - 94 = 29 tenths = 2 9/10 m, matching (b)
(d) says No, comparing 29 tenths with 30 tenths (1/10 m short)

questions.q: A place-value abacus in a Class 7 room has beads for 2 tens, 17 ones, 13 tenths and 25 hundredths. Meena writes the number shown as 21713.25 by putting the counts side by side. Arjun regroups first and writes 38.55. (a) Write the value of each group of beads as a decimal. (b) Add them to find the number shown. (c) Decide who is right and explain exactly what Meena's method gets wrong. (d) Write the number shown as a count of hundredths only.
questions.a: (a) 2 tens = 20, 17 ones = 17, 13 tenths = 1.3, 25 hundredths = 0.25. (b) 20 + 17 + 1.3 + 0.25 = 38.55. (c) Arjun is right. Each place can hold only one digit (0 to 9); 17 ones must be regrouped as 1 ten and 7 ones, 13 tenths as 1 one and 3 tenths, 25 hundredths as 2 tenths and 5 hundredths. Meena's 21713.25 puts the 2 in the ten-thousands place, which is not what 2 tens means. (d) 38.55 = 3855 hundredths.
s: (a) writes the four values 20, 17, 1.3 and 0.25
(b) adds them to get 38.55
(c) says Arjun is right because a place holds one digit, so 17 ones, 13 tenths and 25 hundredths must be regrouped (Meena's digits land in the wrong places)
(d) writes 3855 hundredths

questions.q: Kavya is given the decimal 3.7 and told to write one extra zero into it, in every place it can go: before the 3, between the 3 and the decimal point, just after the decimal point, and after the 7. (a) Write the four new numbers. (b) Which of them are equal to 3.7? Give a place-value reason. (c) For each one that is not equal to 3.7, say whether it is greater or smaller and by how much. (d) State a rule for where a zero can be added to a decimal without changing its value.
questions.a: (a) 03.7, 30.7, 3.07, 3.70. (b) 03.7 and 3.70 equal 3.7: both still have 3 units and 7 tenths; the extra zero sits in an empty place (tens, hundredths). (c) 30.7 is greater by 30.7 - 3.7 = 27, because the 3 moved to the tens place. 3.07 is smaller by 3.7 - 3.07 = 0.63, because the 7 moved to the hundredths place. (d) A zero at the right end after the point, or at the left end before the whole part, does not change the value; a zero put between digits (or between the point and a digit) pushes digits to other places and changes it.
s: (b) picks 03.7 and 3.70, with the reason that the 3 units and 7 tenths stay in their places
(c) 30.7 greater by 27 and 3.07 smaller by 0.63
(d) states the rule: zeros at the ends keep the value, a zero inserted between the point and a digit (or between digits) changes it

questions.q: A number line is drawn from 2 to 4 and the part between 2 and 4 is divided into 10 equal divisions. Point P is at the 3rd division mark after 2 and point Q is at the 7th division mark after 2. (a) What length does each division stand for? (b) Write the numbers at P and Q. (c) The segment from P to the next division mark is zoomed in and divided into 10 equal parts; point R is at the 4th small mark after P. Find R. (d) Rahul says 2.7 cannot be shown on this zoomed segment because its small marks are not tenths. Is he right? Say exactly where 2.7 is.
questions.a: (a) 2 units are split into 10 divisions, so each division is 2/10 = 0.2. (b) three divisions make 0.2 + 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.6, so P = 2.6; seven divisions make 1.4, so Q = 3.4. (c) The zoomed segment runs from 2.6 to 2.8 (length 0.2), so each small part is 0.02; four small parts make 0.08, so R = 2.68. (d) No. 2.7 is 0.1 after 2.6, and 5 small parts of 0.02 make 0.10, so 2.7 is exactly the 5th small mark, the middle of the segment (just right of R).
s: (a) each division is 0.2 (2 units shared into 10 parts)
(c) small part 0.02, so R = 2.68
(d) says Rahul is wrong: 2.7 is the 5th small mark (five parts of 0.02 make 0.1 after 2.6)

questions.q: An electrician in Bhubaneswar has a 3 m reel of wire. For one job she cuts pieces of 85 cm, 1.2 m and 640 mm. (a) Write all three pieces in metres. (b) Find the total length she cut. (c) Find the wire left on the reel in metres, in centimetres and in millimetres. (d) Her next job needs a 35 cm piece. Can she cut it from this reel? Justify with the numbers.
questions.a: (a) 85 cm = 0.85 m; 1.2 m; 640 mm = 64 cm = 0.64 m. (b) 0.85 + 1.2 + 0.64 = 2.69 m. (c) 3 - 2.69 = 0.31 m = 31 cm = 310 mm. (d) No: 31 cm is left and 35 cm is needed, so she is 4 cm short.
s: (a) converts 85 cm to 0.85 m and 640 mm to 0.64 m
(b) total cut 2.69 m
(c) wire left 0.31 m = 31 cm = 310 mm
(d) says No, since 31 cm < 35 cm (4 cm short)

questions.q: A silversmith in Cuttack had 60.25 g of silver and used 37.468 g for an anklet. His apprentice worked out the silver left as 37.218 g. (a) Check the apprentice's answer by adding it back to the silver used. (b) Find the mistake he made in each column. (c) Work out the correct amount left, showing the borrowing from the tenths and the units. (d) Check your answer by addition.
questions.a: (a) 37.218 + 37.468 = 74.686, not 60.25, so his answer is wrong. (b) In every column where the top digit was smaller he took the smaller digit from the larger one instead of borrowing: 8 - 0 = 8 (thousandths, taking 60.25 as 60.250), 6 - 5 = 1, 4 - 2 = 2 and 7 - 0 = 7. (c) 60.250 - 37.468: borrow to get 10 - 8 = 2 thousandths, 14 - 6 = 8 hundredths, 11 - 4 = 7 tenths, then 9 - 7 = 2 units and 5 - 3 = 2 tens: 22.782 g. (d) 22.782 + 37.468 = 60.250 = 60.25.
s: (a) adds 37.218 + 37.468 = 74.686 and says it does not give 60.25
(b) names the mistake: smaller digit taken from larger instead of borrowing (in the thousandths, hundredths, tenths and units columns)
(c) writes 60.25 as 60.250, borrows across the point and gets 22.782 g

questions.q: Sonu's rule says the sum of two decimals is greater than the sum of their whole-number parts and less than that sum plus 2. A trekker in Sikkim walks 8.75 km, 11.4 km and 9.98 km on three days. (a) Extend Sonu's rule to three decimals and give the two whole numbers between which the total must lie. (b) Find the exact total. (c) Her friend's diary shows the total as 32.13 km. Without adding again, show that this cannot be right. (d) Explain why the total can never equal the upper whole number of your range, however large the decimal parts are.
questions.a: (a) Whole parts give 8 + 11 + 9 = 28; each decimal part is less than 1, so the three parts add to less than 3: 28 < total < 31. (b) 8.75 + 11.4 + 9.98 = 30.13 km. (c) 32.13 is more than 31, the largest possible value, so it is impossible. (d) Each decimal part is less than 1, so together they are less than 3; the total is always less than 28 + 3 = 31 and can only come close to it.
s: (a) states 28 < total < 31, using the whole parts 8 + 11 + 9 and the three decimal parts each under 1
(b) exact total 30.13 km
(c) rejects 32.13 because it is above the upper bound 31
(d) explains that three parts each less than 1 add to less than 3, so 31 is never reached

questions.q: In a 50-over school match, Team A's innings lasted 47.4 overs and Team B's innings lasted 45.5 overs, as shown on the scoreboard. (a) Find the number of balls each team faced. (b) How many more balls did Team A face? Write this difference the way a scoreboard writes overs. (c) Priya subtracts 47.4 - 45.5 as decimals and says Team A faced 1.9 overs more. Show why her answer cannot be right. (d) How many balls of its 50 overs did Team A not use? Write this too in scoreboard overs.
questions.a: (a) 47.4 overs = 47 overs and 4 balls = 47 x 6 + 4 = 286 balls; 45.5 overs = 45 x 6 + 5 = 275 balls. (b) 286 - 275 = 11 balls = 1 over and 5 balls, written 1.5 overs. (c) In overs notation the digit after the point counts balls out of 6, so it can only be 0 to 5; '1.9 overs' would mean 9 balls in a part-over, which is impossible. The decimal subtraction treats an over as 10 parts. (d) 50 overs = 300 balls; 300 - 286 = 14 balls = 2 overs and 2 balls, written 2.2 overs.
s: (a) 286 balls for Team A and 275 balls for Team B
(b) 11 balls more, written 1.5 overs
(c) explains that the digit after the point counts balls out of 6, so 1.9 overs is impossible (an over is not 10 parts)
(d) 14 balls unused, written 2.2 overs

questions.q: A school garden club in Shillong records the height of a bean plant every week. The first four readings are 12.35 cm, 12.8 cm, 13.25 cm and 13.7 cm, and the change stays the same each week. (a) Find the change from one week to the next. (b) Write the heights for weeks 5, 6 and 7. (c) In which week does the height first go above 15 cm? (d) Among weeks 1 to 7, which week's height is closest to 14.5 cm? Justify by comparing differences.
questions.a: (a) 12.8 - 12.35 = 0.45 cm each week (13.25 - 12.8 and 13.7 - 13.25 are also 0.45). (b) Week 5: 14.15 cm, week 6: 14.6 cm, week 7: 15.05 cm. (c) Week 7 (15.05 cm); week 6 is only 14.6 cm. (d) Week 6: 14.6 - 14.5 = 0.1, while week 5 is 14.5 - 14.15 = 0.35 away and week 7 is 15.05 - 14.5 = 0.55 away, so 14.6 cm is closest.
s: (a) change of 0.45 cm, checked on the given terms
(c) week 7 is the first above 15 cm
(d) week 6 (14.6 cm), with differences 0.1 against 0.35 and 0.55
